title: Ames Window Risk Register
method: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1. Each risk is a threat event stated as condition and consequence, rated for likelihood and impact on the SP 800-30 qualitative scale (Very Low, Low, Moderate, High, Very High), reduced by controls that are requirements in REQ-2026-001, leaving a residual that someone owns. Response is one of accept, mitigate, transfer, avoid (SP 800-39 §3.4).
scale: Very Low | Low | Moderate | High | Very High, per NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 Appendix G (likelihood) and Appendix H (impact)

risks.title: Network code evades the automated charter checks
risks.statement: If an engineer introduces network capability through a path the tooling does not see, for example a renamed import of the standard library's socket types, then the charter claim 'no network capability' stated in every SVD becomes false without CI noticing.
risks.control_note: deny.toml bans a list of 21 networking crates and denies the network features of two more; it is a list, not a proof, and a networking crate not on it would pass. One locked component for the Linux desktop build, x11rb, contains TCP socket code for remote X displays; whether the application can reach it has not been traced. The CI grep catches the ordinary standard-library and browser forms in our own source. For the browser build, scripts/no-network.sh fails the build if the bundle names a network API and the page's Content-Security-Policy refuses outside connections; for the Windows program, scripts/windows-imports.sh fails if it imports a library outside a short list. Those three are tripwires and the README says what each cannot see. Independent review (REQ-3.2) is practised but not enforced by the repository, so it is not counted as a control here.
risks.review: When REQ-3.2 is enforced (issue #9); when the x11rb path is traced; at each release

risks.title: Unmaintained component in the dependency tree
risks.statement: If a component we ship stops receiving fixes, then a vulnerability found in it later has no upstream remedy and must be handled by replacing the component.
risks.source: RUSTSEC-2026-0192, ttf-parser via winit's Wayland title decorations
risks.control_note: Weekly advisory scan surfaces the condition. Resolved by DM-2026-006: the winit feature that pulled the font parser was replaced, removing the component.
risks.review: Re-opens automatically if cargo deny reports a new unmaintained advisory

risks.title: Compromise of the public component registry
risks.statement: If crates.io, a maintainer account, a build tool installed from crates.io (wasm-bindgen-cli, cargo-cyclonedx) or a GitHub Action used by the workflows is compromised and a malicious version is published, then the next deliberate update, or for tools and Actions the next run, could pull it in. Versions of components already pinned in Cargo.lock are protected by their checksums.
risks.source: Discussion of supply chain threat model, 2026-11-11
risks.control_note: Checksums protect pinned component versions, and only crates.io is an allowed source. None of the controls lowers the chance of adopting a malicious new version: a new version enters on an update, which is a Normal change with review; advisory scanning and the malware scan catch what is already known, after disclosure. Build tools are installed from crates.io at a pinned version on each run with no checksum recorded here, and GitHub Actions are pinned by tag, which can be moved, not by commit. The impact is High because build scripts and procedural macros run on the developer's machine and in the release job, which holds the permissions to sign and publish. Vendoring (cargo vendor) or recorded audits (cargo vet) would prevent it and were considered in DM-2026-005. Independent review (REQ-3.2) is not counted, being unenforced.
risks.review: At each release, or if the project is adopted for a real deployment, when DM-2026-005 is revisited

risks.title: Second-person review is practised but not enforced
risks.statement: If a change is merged to main without review, because nothing in the repository configuration prevents it, then an error or an unwanted change reaches the main line with no second pair of eyes and the audit trail shows no approval.
risks.control_note: No automated control yet. CODEOWNERS is committed; the branch ruleset is a repository setting only the owner can enable.
risks.review: Closes when issue #9 is done and REQ-3.2 and REQ-3.4 carry evidence

risks.title: Documentation drifts from the software it describes
risks.statement: If counts, versions and status quoted in documents and briefings are typed by hand, then they are wrong soon after they are written and an assessor finds the prose contradicting the artifacts.
risks.source: Deck and README numbers were hand-typed before facts.json existed
risks.control_note: sbom.cdx.json, VER-2026-001.md, RISK-2026-001.md and facts.json are generated and drift-checked in CI. The SVD is generated per commit. Prose that quotes a number cites facts.json and the commit it was taken from.
risks.review: When the deck is next regenerated

risks.title: Dependency surface is large relative to the application
risks.statement: If the executable carries far more third-party code than its function needs, mostly platform windowing support, then the attack surface, licence exposure and advisory noise are all larger than necessary, and each component is a place a future vulnerability can appear.
risks.control_note: Inventory and scanning make the surface visible. DM-2026-006 removed the font-parsing subtree. Further reduction means dropping platform features the project does not ship, a Normal change per platform.
risks.review: At each winit or softbuffer update

risks.title: Public repository exposes the process in full
risks.statement: If the repository is public, then every requirement, decision, accepted risk and open item is visible to anyone, including which controls are not yet enforced.
risks.source: Charter: the repository is a compliance demonstration
risks.control_note: Carrying this risk is the better choice. The visibility is the purpose: the method is meant to be lifted into other projects. Mitigating by going private would remove the value entirely, and a half measure (hiding only the open items) would make the record dishonest. The real exposure is bounded by the CM plan boundary: anything that would be CUI for a real deployment, such as named people, devices, destinations or system boundaries, is kept out of this repository by rule. Cost of mitigation: the project. Cost of carrying: none beyond keeping that boundary. The boundary between what may be public and what may not is procedural: nothing scans for a breach of it, and secret scanning is off for the repository.
risks.review: If the repository is ever used as the instance for a real deployment rather than the method; or on any breach of the boundary

risks.title: Single hosting platform for code, issues, releases and CI
risks.statement: If GitHub is unavailable, changes policy, or the account is lost, then the issue trail, release assets and CI history are unreachable until restored, and no change can be merged under the process in the meantime.
risks.control_note: Carrying this risk is the better choice. Git is distributed: every clone holds the full history, the SBOM, the requirements, the register and the generators, so every document except the issue thread is reproducible from any clone with no platform at all. Mitigating with a second platform and a mirror adds a synchronisation process and a second place for records to diverge, which is itself a configuration-management risk. The residual, loss of the issue thread, is reduced by referencing issue conclusions in the decision memoranda, which are in the tree. Cost of mitigation: a mirror, a sync, and a second audit log. Cost of carrying: an outage delays merges and loses nothing permanent that is in the tree. What lives only on the platform, and in no clone: the issue threads, the pull request reviews that are the record of approval, the Human's concurrences, and the build provenance attestations. The 'every clone is a copy' argument rests today on one owner and no forks.
risks.review: Annually, or if the repository becomes the system of record for a real deployment

risks.title: Duplicate versions of the same component in the tree
risks.statement: If several versions of one component are compiled in because different dependencies pin different ranges, then the executable carries redundant code, each copy is a separate place for a vulnerability to appear, and advisory scanning may flag a version that a newer sibling has already fixed.
risks.source: cargo deny bans: warning[duplicate] on about a dozen components at 2026-11-11
risks.control_note: Scanning covers every copy, so nothing is missed, but the surface is larger than it needs to be. Planned mitigation: a reviewed cargo update as a Normal change, reconciling versions where the dependency graph allows, with a decision memorandum recording what could not be reconciled and why. This risk is carried deliberately into the first release so that the next release can show a risk opened, fixed, closed and every submittal regenerated.
risks.review: At the first release after v0.1.0
